title: Efficacy and safety of minocycline in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (EMPHASIS): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
summary: At 58 Chinese centers, EMPHASIS randomized 1,724 patients with ischemic stroke within 72 hours and NIHSS 4-25 to a short oral minocycline course or placebo plus usual care. Excellent 90-day functional outcome (mRS 0-1) occurred in 447/850 (52.6%) versus 403/851 (47.4%); adjusted RR 1.11 (95% CI 1.03-1.20; P=.0061). Serious adverse events were 4.6% versus 5.9% (P=.24).
findings: Ordinal mRS shift adjusted common OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03-1.38).
Later MIST-A phase 2 trial in a distinct successfully thrombectomized group had no infarct-growth benefit.
comparator: Oral placebo adjunct to usual care.
population: Acute ischemic stroke within 72 hours in 58 Chinese hospitals, baseline NIHSS 4-25; 1,724 randomized.
shortTitle: EMPHASIS adjunct minocycline for ischemic stroke
limitations: Median NIHSS was 5 and few participants received reperfusion, limiting generalization to severe stroke and post-thrombectomy populations. The later MIST-A study is not a direct replication. Primary abstract only, not full Lancet text, was reviewed.
intervention: Short-course oral minocycline adjunct begun within 72 hours in trial.
whyItMatters: Promising adjunctive evidence for stroke-service discussion, not a reason to start routine ED minocycline or delay reperfusion assessment. A later trial among successfully thrombectomized patients did not improve its separate infarct-growth endpoint.
evidenceNotes: Primary PubMed abstract PMID 41628627 DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01862-8 reviewed; Epub January 30, 2026 rather than February 14 print. Lancet full text not reviewed. Later primary MIST-A abstract PMID 42305108 consulted for distinct subgroup evidence; no specific correction verified by targeted search.
